content:
maya: Heads-up: eu-west GPU pool saturated and we're seeing admission backpressure. Can folks look?
jack: seeing 503s in the gateway, plus a lot of queued tokens in the admission metrics. dashboard -> https://dash.redwood.internal/runs/ops/1763 :grimacing: 
ana: pushing to incident channel. Any recent deploys to autoscaler or admission? @jack did you touch admission-controller config?
jack: I updated admission thresholds yesterday for burst handling but reverted most changes. I did change the region routing policy for fallbacks.
ronnie: eu-west GPU utilization is at 98% for the last 20m. queue_length metric spiked from 50->1200 in ~3m.
ops-bot: Incident CREATED: gpu-pool-saturation-eu-west (sev-2) — responders: maya, jack, ana, ronnie.
sre-lead: quick triage: are we seeing cross-region routing? fallback to us-east? That could cascade.
maya: yes, logs show admission controller started rejecting localized requests and routing them to global fallback pool in us-east. us-east queue jumped soon after.
jack: autoscaler in us-east did NOT scale. Looking at scaler logs: it failed to find matching nodepool label because the nodepool label changed in the last infra PR. Oops.
ana: so a misconfigured node label prevented scale up -> inability to absorb fallback traffic -> queueing + timeouts cascade.
ronnie: also noticed network egress from eu-west to us-east peaked, saturating inter-region links for 2 minutes. Might have added extra latency.
maya: capturing timeline: 11:10 root cause event (eu-west hitting 95%), 11:11 admission fallback routing enabled, 11:12 us-east queue spike, 11:13 autoscaler error, 11:15 packet-lag and more 503s.
jack: logs excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T11:12:02Z] admission-controller: route_fallback(region=eu-west)->us-east, reason=pool_capacity_exhausted
[2026-03-15T11:12:04Z] autoscaler: scale_request(nodepool=high-gpu, label=env:prod) -> error: no nodes match label env:prod
[2026-03-15T11:13:05Z] serving-runtime: enqueue(token_count=2300) -> queue_len=1200
```
ana: that autoscaler label change came from infra PR #482. Tagging @jack @ronnie to confirm.
jack: confirmed, PR changed label from env:prod to environment:prod to match new naming. Scaler still expects old key. I rolled a hotfix to revert label mapping at 11:20.
ronnie: mitigation steps we did: 1) disabled cross-region fallback (11:16) to stop new traffic flowing to us-east, 2) manually scaled up a reserve pool in us-east (11:18), 3) patched autoscaler label mapping (11:20), 4) drained queued requests via temporary increased timeouts (11:22).
sre-lead: good. What else caused initial saturation in eu-west? sudden traffic spike? model hot cache miss?
maya: preliminary: scheduled nightly batch inference overlapped with customer batch job at 11:05. Batching patterns aligned and KV cache miss percentage rose (cache eviction due to recent model rollout).
jack: oh right — there was a small model variant rollout at 10:50 in eu-west that increased memory pressure -> cache evictions. That combined with batch job increased per-request token work.
ana: so multi-factor: model rollout -> cache miss -> increased token compute -> pool approaches capacity -> admission kicks fallback -> misconfigured autoscaler + network saturation -> cascade.
ronnie: cost note: we had to spin up emergency on-demand GPUs in us-east for ~40m. Estimate ~ $1.8k additional for the incident window.
maya: postmortem action items I'm adding now: 
- Rollback policy: stricter preflight for model rollouts that change memory footprint (owner: eng-ml).
- Autoscaler config: accept both label keys or be driven by nodepool id, add unit tests (owner: eng-infra).
- Admission controller: add circuit-breaker that stops cross-region fallback if downstream queue > X (owner: runtime).
- Scheduling: avoid heavy batch jobs during model rollouts; add scheduler window enforcement (owner: platform).
- Network: add alert for inter-region egress > threshold (owner: cloud-net).
- Cost / billing: finance to reconcile emergency spend (owner: finance).
jack: I'll open the autoscaler PR and tests today. linking infra PR that caused label rename: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/482
ana: adding runbook update: runbook should include steps: disable fallback, verify autoscaler labels, manual scale, drain.
sre-lead: assign owners and target dates. I'd like a follow-up 30-min blameless postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT.
maya: thanks everyone. please add any additional notes in the postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/postmortems/1763005000-regional-admission-misconfig-fanout
jack: quick note: we should add an automated integration test that simulates fallback traffic to verify autoscaler behavior.
ronnie: noted. also propose adding a short-term safeguard: if fallback rate > 20% for >2m, pause new rollouts in that region.
maya: ack. marking incident as RESOLVED at 11:37 after queues drained and autoscaler healthy. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident RESOLVED: gpu-pool-saturation-eu-west — duration 27m.
